chunks: My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said: Al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) said:
O Ishaq! Soften your speech with the hypocrite, be sincere in your love for the believer, and if a Jew sits with you, then be gracious in his company.

key_terms.المنافق: Hypocrite - one who outwardly professes faith but harbors disbelief; the Imam advises civil dealings with such people rather than confrontation
key_terms.صانع: To deal gently, to be diplomatic in speech (musana'a) - refers to measured, courteous speech without necessarily believing in the other person's sincerity
key_terms.مجالسته: His company/sitting together - refers to the etiquette of shared gatherings and social interaction
key_terms.ود: Sincere affection, heartfelt love - deeper than mere politeness; reserved exclusively for the true believer

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about treating non-Muslims and hypocrites?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) addresses his companion Ishaq ibn Ammar with a teaching on interpersonal conduct. The Imam instructs that one should deal diplomatically with hypocrites through measured speech, reserve genuine affection for the faithful, and extend gracious hospitality even to non-Muslims such as Jews. This teaching, delivered in a private session, reflects the broader Islamic ethic of treating all people with dignity while maintaining sincerity of heart for fellow believers.
